reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E4) directly supports the formation of an a-C tribolayer from ethanol via catalytic activity of the specific 2D HEA nanoflakes, and E4 confirms the spray-coating feasibility. E3 reinforces the necessity of ethanol for performance. All key premises are accurately represented and well-supported by the provided passages.
premises: 2D HEA nanoflakes are catalytically active and can dissociate organic molecules during sliding.
The catalytic dissociation of ethanol by 2D HEA nanoflakes forms an amorphous carbon (a-C) tribolayer.
The a-C tribolayer reduces friction and wear by lowering shear forces and preventing metal-metal contact.
The spray-coating of 2D HEA nanoflakes is a feasible method to apply the lubricant to surfaces.
The beneficial effect requires trace organic species (e.g., ethanol) as a carbon source.
